newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Leftover funds spur mid-term Russian paper.
newsitem.headline: Leftover funds spur mid-term Russian paper.

text.p: securities got a boost of 0.3-0.4 percentage point at the post-auction trading because of higher liquidity and before a long holiday, dealers said.

They said demand was spurred by a big volume of funds left over after Wednesday's auctions for GKO discount Treasury bills and OFZ interest-bearing bonds auctions and by banks' unwillingness to stay in cash over holidays.
Russian markets will be closed May 1-4. There was a one-hour trading session after the auctions. Usually trading sessions are not held on Wednesdays.
"The fact that the rise was mainly in medium-term paper testifies to the fact that the demand was mostly Russian," said Raiffeisen Bank Oesterreich dealer Alexander Losev.
Dealers forecast a moderate correction after the holidays as market participants were unlikely to set aside significant money for Monday over the holiday period.
"The absence of trading during the holidays will increase the yield automatically, and if there is a small remnant of funds in the system prices may slip," Losev said.
